newsitem.title: USA: BMW 1996 U.S. sales top 105,000 units.
newsitem.headline: BMW 1996 U.S. sales top 105,000 units.

text.p: BMW of North America Inc said Monday its 1996 U.S. sales exceeded the 100,000-unit mark for the first time in the company's history, ending the year at 105,761 cars.
That represents a 12.6 percent increase over the 93,309 cars BMW sold in the United States during 1995, based on daily selling rates. BMW gave the figures in a statement.

During December, BMW said its sales totaled 6,501 cars, down 10.2 percent from the December 1995 total of 7,238 cars. BMW said, however, that it closed its December reporting period on December 24, 1996, shortening the selling period for the month by a week.

Bayerische Motoren Werke AG said its worldwide sales for 1996 were up about nine percent over the prior year, for a total exceeding 640,000 vehicles. Combined BMW and Rover Group sales for 1996 will be "substantially more than 1.1 million vehicles worldwide," the company said.
Rover figures, which will exceed 500,000 units, will be announced on Tuesday, BMW said.
